_status.added_by_the_server: serve/models.py's GLM profile appends --eos-ids 154820,154827,154829 and --turn-token 154828 (<|assistant|>) to args; the engine's defaults (248044,248046 and 248045) are Qwen ids
_status.engine_path: src/program/glm_serve.cpp (wave 6): the GLM serve loop speaks generate.cpp's protocol (GEN, T, PP, RESUME, REUSED, DONE, STOP, QUIT); decode windows of 1 token (no --mtp, no --spec: no GLM drafter); prompt parts of more than --short-read 64 tokens go through the prompt path, shorter ones through windows of 1
_status.context: --max-context 262144 with --kv-resident 32768: the DSA latent cache keeps 32,768 cells per layer in VRAM and every cell in page-locked RAM (11 layers x 262,144 x 1,056 B = 2,904 MiB); the session is 706 MiB of VRAM (fully resident it would be 3,246 MiB). The decode windows stream the pages they select; the prompt path reads pages that are not in VRAM from the host copy (glm-mini: identical output, -2% prompt speed at 76K; not yet measured on the 3090)
_status.glm_pool_off: window 3 on epyc: --glm-pool auto chose the CPU pool and decoded at 5.90 tok/s, staging (off) at 7.05
_status.sampling: the llama profile's (docker-compose.yml: temp 1.0, top-p 0.95, min-p 0.0) plus top_k 40, llama.cpp's default that profile runs with (without it the engine's own default, 20, applies)
_status.ram: 67 GiB experts + 2.8 GiB DSA host copy + up to 2.8 GiB file-tier slots + 4 GiB parked conversations + up to 6 x 153 MB turn checkpoints, on 94 GiB
_status.disk_tier: its own directory, and the engine adds arch=glm5-next to its fingerprint and tags the image geometry, so Qwen and GLM entries never match; a GLM image is 152.6 MB of KDA state per checkpoint plus 12,320 B per token
